skills.name: Distance formula
skills.wrong_turn: Square, add, then take the root. √(3² + 4²) = 5, not 3 + 4 = 7.

skills.name: Midpoint formula

steps.d: center of a circle from a diameter

skills.wrong_turn: The midpoint adds, it doesn't subtract: for (2, 6) and (8, 10) it is (5, 8), not (3, 2).

skills.name: Partition a segment
skills.wrong_turn: Ratio 1 : 3 means 1/4 of the way, not 1/3. The parts are 1 and 3 out of 4.
skills.rule: To split AB in the ratio a:b, go t=(aa+b) of the way: P=A+t(B−A).

skills.name: Slope criteria
skills.wrong_turn: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals, not just negatives: perpendicular to 2/3 is −3/2, not −2/3.

skills.name: Special lines
skills.wrong_turn: A median goes to the midpoint of the opposite side; an altitude meets it at a right angle. They coincide only in special triangles.
skills.rule: Perpendicular bisector: midpoint, perpendicular. Altitude: vertex, perpendicular to the opposite side. Median: vertex to opposite midpoint.

skills.name: Perimeter & area on the plane
skills.wrong_turn: The shoelace formula needs the vertices in order around the shape. Jump across the polygon and the area comes out wrong.
skills.rule: Perimeter: add the side lengths. Area: box and subtract, or use the shoelace formula.

skills.name: Point-to-line distance
skills.wrong_turn: Write the line as ax + by + c = 0 first: y = 2x + 3 becomes 2x − y + 3 = 0, so b = −1, not 1.
skills.rule: The distance from (x0,y0) to ax+by+c=0 is d=(|ax0+by0+c|a2+b2).

skills.name: Classify by coordinates
skills.wrong_turn: Four equal sides don't make a square: a rhombus has them too. You still need a right angle.
skills.rule: Distance tests equal sides, slope tests parallel and perpendicular, midpoints test bisecting diagonals.

skills.name: Coordinate proofs of triangles
skills.wrong_turn: Specific numbers like (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3) prove the claim for one triangle only. A general proof needs letters.
skills.rule: Put a vertex at the origin and a side on the x-axis, and use letters for the other coordinates.
